finding.description: Describes a defect in the same-role review, not a candidate defect already captured by a supported review finding.

reviewFindingAdjudication.description: Judges one finding made by the same-role review rather than judging the candidate defect again.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain why this review finding is rejected; this array is empty when judgment is supported.

surfaceAdjudication.description: Echoes the bound same-role review assessment in reviewAssessmentJudgment and judges the soundness of that assessment in judgment. A sound blocking review assessment is blocking plus supported, not an adjudication failure.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain a rejected same-role review assessment. It is empty for supported; rejected requires a linked blocking finding on this surface.

judgment.description: supported approves the same-role review assessment even when reviewAssessmentJudgment is blocking; rejected means the assessment is unsound or incomplete.

reviewAssessmentJudgment.description: Exact echo of the bound same-role review assessment's judgment; the deterministic verifier rejects any mismatch.

adjudicationSchema.description: This record judges the soundness and completeness of the same-role review, not the candidate.

findings.description: Adjudicator findings describe defects in the same-role review's requirement, assessment, reasoning, finding, coverage, or severity; they do not repeat candidate defects already captured by supported review findings.

reviewFindingAdjudications.description: Each entry judges one same-role review finding. A supported review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected review finding requires a linked blocking adjudicator finding that explains the review defect.

surfaceAdjudications.description: Each entry exactly echoes the same-role review assessment's pass, advisory, or blocking judgment, then separately judges that assessment as supported or rejected; it does not judge the candidate surface directly.

verdict.description: pass means the same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate; fail means the same-role review is unsound or incomplete. This verdict never judges the candidate directly.

adjudicationSchema.title: Independent canonical-English semantic adjudication record

adjudicationSemantics.failMeaning: The same-role review is unsound or incomplete.
adjudicationSemantics.findingLinkMeaning: A supported surface assessment or review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected one links at least one blocking adjudicator finding on an overlapping surface that explains a defect in the review.
adjudicationSemantics.passMeaning: The same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate.
adjudicationSemantics.subject: same-role-review
adjudicationSemantics.surfaceAdjudicationMeaning: Each surface adjudication exactly echoes the bound review assessment judgment in reviewAssessmentJudgment, then uses judgment supported or rejected to judge that assessment.

The problem: a downloaded file does not identify a training corpus An LLM learns from the text supplied to its training pipeline. A filename alone does not tell you which text was supplied. Two files named train.txt can contain different bytes, and a complete download can still come from the wrong source revision. Even the right text is insufficient for a reproducible corpus record if its source, license text or attribution has been lost. The acquisition boundary needs two kinds of evidence together: a record of the selected sources and their provenance, and checks that the available files match that record. This chapter builds that boundary. It does not clean the text, choose final training splits or establish that the corpus is safe or useful.
Start with a complete, tiny corpus bundle The example uses course-authored test bytes, not a downloaded training dataset. It has two raw text sources and two shared provenance files: File in the bundle | Exact bytes represented as a Rust literal | Byte count raw/train.txt | b"abc" | 3 raw/valid.txt | b"hello
" | 6 provenance/LICENSE.txt | b"fixture-only
" | 13 provenance/ATTRIBUTION.txt | b"course-authored fixture
" | 24 In these literals, 
 represents one newline byte, not a backslash followed by the letter n. The two raw sources contain 3+6=9 bytes. The four payload files in the table contain 3+6+13+24=46 bytes; this count excludes the manifest record introduced below. Both source records refer to the same license and attribution files, so those shared files are counted once in the inventory. The fixture’s license identifier is LicenseRef-Course-Test-Only. Its records mark redistribution as not-approved. Those values describe this test fixture; they do not grant permission for a real corpus or a model trained from one. Likewise, the name valid.txt identifies a raw held-out source here, not the final validation split that a later chapter will construct.
The solution: identify the record, then verify every file A manifest is the record describing the bundle. Each payload entry names a relative path, a role, a media type, an exact byte count and a SHA-256 digest. Each source record also identifies the selected source revision, requested URL, resolved endpoint, license and attribution. These fields connect a source to its bytes and provenance instead of leaving them as unrelated notes. The manifest receives one fixed byte representation: compact UTF-8 JSON, object keys in byte-sorted order, declared array order and exactly one final newline. That representation is called canonical. Its purpose is to prevent harmless formatting choices, such as indentation, from giving the same record multiple identities. An incoming manifest with a different representation is rejected; the verifier does not quietly rewrite it. The bundle identity is \mathrm{artifact\_id}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes})
What the identity formula means Here \mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes} means the complete canonical record, including the payload digests and source provenance. \operatorname{SHA256} maps those bytes to a 256-bit digest. \mathrm{artifact\_id} is that digest, usually displayed as 64 hexadecimal characters. It identifies the record; it is not a signature or a certificate of legal permission, privacy or language quality. The raw files are represented in the identity through their recorded byte counts and digests. The verifier must still read the actual files and compare them with those entries. Hashing a manifest does not prove that its claimed files exist. The verifier performs three checks in order: Validate the manifest against the selected source policy, including both raw sources and their provenance references. Check the payload inventory. All four listed files must exist as regular, non-linked files; missing or unlisted files cause refusal. Read each file in bounded chunks, count its bytes and calculate its digest. Accept the bundle only when every count and digest matches. SHA-256 calculation and JSON parsing use supporting libraries. Rust owns the course-specific source policy, inventory checks, byte comparisons and admission decision. Rust checks the observed byte count and digest separately, reading at most one bounded chunk at a time and probing for actual end of file. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/inventory.rs#bounded-payload-verification pub fn verify_payload( expected: &PayloadEntry, reader: &mut impl Read, ) -> Result<VerifiedPayload, AcquisitionError> { let mut hasher = Sha256::new(); let mut buffer = [0_u8; STREAM_BUFFER_BYTES]; let mut total = 0_u64; loop { // Once expected bytes have arrived, one additional byte distinguishes // a real EOF from a same-prefix oversize object. Never retain that byte. let remaining = expected .bytes .checked_sub(total) .ok_or(AcquisitionError::Size)?; let allowance = remaining.min(STREAM_BUFFER_BYTES as u64) as usize; let count = loop { match reader.read(&mut buffer[..allowance.max(1)]) { Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue, result => break result.map_err(|_| AcquisitionError::Io)?, } }; if count == 0 { break; } total = total .checked_add(count as u64) .ok_or(AcquisitionError::Size)?; if total > expected.bytes { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } hasher.update(&buffer[..count]); } if total != expected.bytes { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } let digest = format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize()); if digest != expected.sha256 { return Err(AcquisitionError::Hash); } Ok(VerifiedPayload { path: expected.path.clone(), bytes: total, sha256: digest, }) } Two changes that expose the boundary Replacing b"abc" with b"abd" preserves the train file’s 3-byte length. A size-only check accepts the replacement. The full verifier rejects it with Hash, because the observed digest differs from the selected manifest entry. This is a file-byte check, not evidence about what either text would teach a model. Changing the attribution file to b"course-authored fixture v2
" instead changes that file to 27 bytes. Rebuilding a consistent manifest updates its attribution entry and both sources’ attribution references. The resulting bundle identity differs, although the two raw text digests remain unchanged. The new complete payload totals 49 bytes. The identity therefore distinguishes provenance changes as well as raw-text changes. Selected fields from the actual offline fixture report are shown below. The manifest occupies 3084 bytes separately from the 46 payload bytes. The scope value keeps this result identified as a synthetic fixture, not an acquired training dataset. { "artifact_id": "569de16c16720f73aca07de6a3184b779b80700c3f5f8eefc01f60fea3019b89", "artifact_manifest_bytes": 3084, "inventoried_files": 4, "logical_sources": 2, "raw_bytes": 9, "scope": "synthetic-offline-fixture", "total_payload_bytes": 46 } The offline Rust report separates bundle identity, verified file bytes, restart accounting and the fixture's limited scope. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs#governed-report Ok(serde_json::json!({ "artifact_id": verified.artifact_id(), "artifact_manifest_bytes": canonical_manifest_bytes(&manifest)?.len(), "attribution_variant_artifact_id": artifact_id(&variant)?.as_hex(), "budget_case": { "acknowledged_body_bytes": budget.progress().acknowledged_body_bytes()?, "attempts_after_refusal": budget.progress().attempts(0), "ceiling_bytes": 10, "remaining_raw_bytes": 9, "projected_required_bytes": 11, "refusal": budget_refusal.to_string(), "dispatch_permitted": false }, "checks": { "attribution_change_changes_bundle_identity": artifact_id(&manifest)? != artifact_id(&variant)?, "attribution_change_preserves_raw_digests": manifest.sources.iter().zip(&variant.sources).all(|(a,b)| a.sha256 == b.sha256), "complete_bundle_replay_identity": replay.artifact_id() == verified.artifact_id(), "same_size_wrong_bytes_refusal": corrupted.unwrap_err().to_string(), "size_only_contrast_accepts_abd": b"abd".len() as u64 == raw_train.bytes }, "files": verified.files().iter().map(|file| serde_json::json!({ "bytes": file.bytes(), "path": file.path(), "sha256": file.sha256() })).collect::<Vec<_>>(), "inventoried_files": 4, "logical_sources": 2, "privacy_quality_or_redistribution_approval": false, "raw_bytes": 9, "resume": { "acknowledged_body_bytes": store.progress().acknowledged_body_bytes()?, "attempts": [store.progress().attempts(0), store.progress().attempts(1)], "complete_pair": store.progress().is_complete(), "uncertain_body_bytes": store.progress().uncertain_body_bytes() }, "schema_version": 1, "scope": "synthetic-offline-fixture", "total_payload_bytes": verified.total_bytes() })) The example executable runs only this offline fixture and prints its report. It does not download a training corpus. The example runs the offline corpus fixture and prints its checked report; it performs no real corpus download. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/main.rs#offline-acquisition-example fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { // The executable has no HTTP transport and no production acquisition mode. let report = run_fixture()?; println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)?); Ok(()) }
Interrupted acquisition must not erase earlier work Acquisition can stop between receiving bytes and completing a source. A resumed request must continue the same selected source and preserve the acquisition’s limits; starting a new process must not grant a new byte budget or deadline. In the fixture, the first request retains b"ab", a 2-byte prefix of the 3-byte train source. After restart, Rust rehashes that retained prefix and checks its recorded digest. The next request asks for the byte at offset 2, where offsets start at zero. Its response must cover exactly bytes 2-2/3 and carry the same strong entity tag as the first response. The entity tag is the server’s representation validator; it ties the resumed response to the earlier response, while the final SHA-256 check ties the assembled bytes to the selected source policy. Receiving b"c" brings the retained length to 3 bytes, but completion still requires an explicit end-of-body observation and the final digest check. The held-out source is then checked separately. The report records 9 acknowledged body bytes and request-attempt counts [2,1]: two attempts for the train source, one for the held-out source. A complete train source alone is not a complete pair. Body bytes that were read and discarded still consume the transfer budget. For a separate toy ceiling of 10 bytes, an error response that delivers 2 discarded bytes leaves only 8 bytes available. The two raw sources still require 9 bytes, so the next request is refused before dispatch: 2+9=11>10. Rust reserves a bounded body-read grant before allowing transport to read. If a process stops with an unsettled grant, recovery charges the whole grant as uncertain delivery, once, rather than assuming that no bytes were read. This conservative rule may prevent further acquisition even when fewer bytes actually arrived. It prevents uncertainty from becoming free budget. The counter measures bytes delivered through this body-read interface, not every byte buffered by the operating system or every network packet. Corrupt retained prefixes are refused and preserved in quarantine. Recovery does not reset the attempt count, charged bytes or original deadline. These safeguards make interruption visible; they do not turn a failed attempt into an admitted corpus.
History: retain the dataset’s context, not just its filename The useful intuition behind a filename-and-size inventory is simple: record which files were expected and detect missing or truncated downloads. Its limitation is visible in the abc to abd example: the name and size can agree while the text differs. That Rust comparison is a deliberately limited baseline, not a claim that historical dataset projects relied only on file sizes. A file inventory alone does not preserve a dataset’s collection context, provenance or suitability for language-model training. Datasheets for Datasets proposes structured dataset documentation; the later ROOTS corpus describes source selection, metadata and governance for a multilingual language-model corpus. Datasheets for Datasets was first posted in 2018. Gebru and colleagues propose documentation covering a dataset’s motivation, composition, collection, preprocessing, uses, distribution and maintenance. That documentation supports informed decisions by dataset creators and users; a checksum cannot replace it. The BigScience ROOTS Corpus is described in a 2023 preprint. The ROOTS corpus paper describes source selection, metadata and governance in construction of a multilingual language-model corpus; it does not validate this chapter’s fixture. The tiny manifest is not an implementation of the ROOTS governance process or proof of a dataset’s suitability. Keep selected corpus bytes linked to their source context before downstream filtering, split construction and training. Byte agreement does not establish quality, privacy or permission.
Read the evidence directly A spatial diagram would not make this example’s decisions clearer. The file table states exactly which bytes belong to each role, and the Rust report records the changed identity, digest refusal and restart counts directly. Read those values together: the manifest identifies a complete record, byte verification checks its files, and the scope field identifies the result as a synthetic fixture.
Optional practice: reproduce and explain the checks Run size_digest_truncation_and_overrun_are_separate_failures and inspect the abd case. Explain why its length passes but its bytes are refused. Run provenance_changes_identity_without_changing_raw_digests. Identify the records that change when the attribution gains v2. Run actual_error_body_consumes_budget_without_retaining_payload. Explain why discarding the error text does not permit a fresh request under the toy ceiling. Checked explanations for the three corpus-verification tasks The manifest expects 3 bytes, so length alone cannot distinguish abc from abd. Their digests differ; the full verifier returns Hash rather than publishing the replacement as the selected corpus. The attribution payload entry changes its count and digest, and both source records change their attribution digest. The raw train and held-out digests remain unchanged. The complete manifest changes, so its artifact identity changes too. The 2 delivered error bytes remain charged. With 9 raw bytes still needed, projected delivery is 11 bytes, above the 10-byte ceiling. The refused request does not increment attempts or create a payload partial.
What this supplies to the decoder pipeline The scalar reference remains unchanged. This chapter supplies a way to identify and verify a complete corpus input before later filtering and tokenization. The offline example has not acquired TinyStories. Real acquisition needs its selected source records and approved provenance; Chapter 42’s filtering work must consume that verified real input, not relabel this fixture as training data. Verification answers whether the selected record and available bytes agree. Quality, privacy, contamination and final split selection remain separate questions.

Open cheat sheet
Canonical manifest A complete corpus record with one fixed byte representation, including file paths, roles, counts, digests and source provenance. The verifier rejects a different representation rather than silently rewriting it.
Corpus bundle The selected raw text sources together with their manifest and provenance files. In this offline fixture, two raw sources share one license file and one attribution file.
Dataset artifact identity The SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical manifest. It identifies the corpus record through its provenance and recorded file digests; actual files still need verification. It is not a signature or permission certificate.
Raw held-out source The separately acquired text source reserved from the raw training source. Its source filename does not define the final course validation or test split.
Retained source prefix The initial bytes of one selected raw source that have been stored and recorded during incomplete acquisition. Recovery rehashes those bytes; resumed delivery must match the same representation validator and final source digest.
Source provenance The record connecting selected corpus bytes to their source revision, requested and resolved endpoints, license text and attribution. It does not by itself establish permission or suitability.

<h2 id="the-problem-a-downloaded-file-does-not-identify-a-training-corpus">The problem: a downloaded file does not identify a training corpus</h2>
<p>An LLM learns from the text supplied to its training pipeline. A filename alone
does not tell you which text was supplied. Two files named <code>train.txt</code> can contain
different bytes, and a complete download can still come from the wrong source
revision. Even the right text is insufficient for a reproducible corpus record
if its source, license text or attribution has been lost.</p>
<p>The acquisition boundary needs two kinds of evidence together: a record of the
selected sources and their provenance, and checks that the available files match
that record. This chapter builds that boundary. It does not clean the text,
choose final training splits or establish that the corpus is safe or useful.</p>

It has two raw text sources and two shared provenance files:</p>

<p>The fixture’s license identifier is <code>LicenseRef-Course-Test-Only</code>. Its records
mark redistribution as <code>not-approved</code>. Those values describe this test fixture;

final validation split that a later chapter will construct.</p>

<h2 id="the-solution-identify-the-record-then-verify-every-file">The solution: identify the record, then verify every file</h2>
<p>A <strong>manifest</strong> is the record describing the bundle. Each payload entry names a
relative path, a role, a media type, an exact byte count and a SHA-256 digest.
Each source record also identifies the selected source revision, requested URL,
resolved endpoint, license and attribution. These fields connect a source to
its bytes and provenance instead of leaving them as unrelated notes.</p>
<p>The manifest receives one fixed byte representation: compact UTF-8 JSON, object
keys in byte-sorted order, declared array order and exactly one final newline.
That representation is called <strong>canonical</strong>. Its purpose is to prevent harmless
formatting choices, such as indentation, from giving the same record multiple
identities. An incoming manifest with a different representation is rejected;
the verifier does not quietly rewrite it.</p>
<p>The bundle identity is</p>

<h2 id="what-the-identity-formula-means">What the identity formula means</h2>
<p>Here <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0044em;vertical-align:-0.31em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm">canonical_manifest_bytes</span></span></span></span></span> means the complete canonical record,
including the payload digests and source provenance.
<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">SHA256</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{SHA256}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6833em"></span><span class="mop"><span class="mord mathrm">SHA256</span></span></span></span></span> maps those bytes to a <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">256</span></span></span></span>-bit digest.
<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">_</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{artifact\_id}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0044em;vertical-align:-0.31em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathrm">artifact_id</span></span></span></span></span> is that digest, usually displayed as <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">64</span></span></span></span> hexadecimal
characters. It identifies the record; it is not a signature or a certificate
of legal permission, privacy or language quality.</p>
<p>The raw files are represented in the identity through their recorded byte counts
and digests. The verifier must still read the actual files and compare them with
those entries. Hashing a manifest does not prove that its claimed files exist.</p>
<p>The verifier performs three checks in order:</p>
<ol>
<li>Validate the manifest against the selected source policy, including both raw
sources and their provenance references.</li>
<li>Check the payload inventory. All four listed files must exist as regular,
non-linked files; missing or unlisted files cause refusal.</li>
<li>Read each file in bounded chunks, count its bytes and calculate its digest.
Accept the bundle only when every count and digest matches.</li>
</ol>

<p>SHA-256 calculation and JSON parsing use supporting libraries. Rust owns the
course-specific source policy, inventory checks, byte comparisons and admission
decision.</p>

<h3 id="two-changes-that-expose-the-boundary">Two changes that expose the boundary</h3>
<p>Replacing <code>b"abc"</code> with <code>b"abd"</code> preserves the train file’s <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span>-byte length.
A size-only check accepts the replacement. The full verifier rejects it with
<code>Hash</code>, because the observed digest differs from the selected manifest entry.
This is a file-byte check, not evidence about what either text would teach a model.</p>
<p>Changing the attribution file to <code>b"course-authored fixture v2\n"</code> instead
changes that file to <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>27</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">27</span></span></span></span> bytes. Rebuilding a consistent manifest updates its
attribution entry and both sources’ attribution references. The resulting
bundle identity differs, although the two raw text digests remain unchanged.
The new complete payload totals <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>49</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">49</span></span></span></span> bytes. The identity therefore distinguishes
provenance changes as well as raw-text changes.</p>
<p>Selected fields from the actual offline fixture report are shown below. The
manifest occupies <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3084</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3084</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3084</span></span></span></span> bytes separately from the <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>46</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">46</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">46</span></span></span></span> payload bytes. The scope
value keeps this result identified as a synthetic fixture, not an acquired
training dataset.</p>

<h2 id="interrupted-acquisition-must-not-erase-earlier-work">Interrupted acquisition must not erase earlier work</h2>
<p>Acquisition can stop between receiving bytes and completing a source. A resumed
request must continue the same selected source and preserve the acquisition’s
limits; starting a new process must not grant a new byte budget or deadline.</p>
<p>In the fixture, the first request retains <code>b"ab"</code>, a <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span>-byte prefix of the
<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span>-byte train source. After restart, Rust rehashes that retained prefix and
checks its recorded digest. The next request asks for the byte at offset <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span>,
where offsets start at zero. Its response must cover exactly <code>bytes 2-2/3</code> and
carry the same strong entity tag as the first response. The entity tag is the
server’s representation validator; it ties the resumed response to the earlier
response, while the final SHA-256 check ties the assembled bytes to the selected
source policy.</p>
<p>Receiving <code>b"c"</code> brings the retained length to <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span> bytes, but completion still
requires an explicit end-of-body observation and the final digest check. The
held-out source is then checked separately. The report records <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">9</span></span></span></span> acknowledged
body bytes and request-attempt counts <code>[2,1]</code>: two attempts for the train source,
one for the held-out source. A complete train source alone is not a complete pair.</p>
<p>Body bytes that were read and discarded still consume the transfer budget.
For a separate toy ceiling of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">10</span></span></span></span> bytes, an error response that delivers
<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> discarded bytes leaves only <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">8</span></span></span></span> bytes available. The two raw sources still
require <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">9</span></span></span></span> bytes, so the next request is refused before dispatch:</p>
<span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>></mo><mn>10.</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2+9=11>10.</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em"></span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">9</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6835em;vertical-align:-0.0391em"></span><span class="mord">11</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span><span class="mrel">></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">10.</span></span></span></span></span>
<p>Rust reserves a bounded body-read grant before allowing transport to read. If a
process stops with an unsettled grant, recovery charges the whole grant as
uncertain delivery, once, rather than assuming that no bytes were read. This
conservative rule may prevent further acquisition even when fewer bytes actually
arrived. It prevents uncertainty from becoming free budget. The counter measures
bytes delivered through this body-read interface, not every byte buffered by the
operating system or every network packet.</p>
<p>Corrupt retained prefixes are refused and preserved in quarantine. Recovery does
not reset the attempt count, charged bytes or original deadline. These safeguards
make interruption visible; they do not turn a failed attempt into an admitted
corpus.</p>

<h2 id="history-retain-the-datasets-context-not-just-its-filename">History: retain the dataset’s context, not just its filename</h2>
<p>The useful intuition behind a filename-and-size inventory is simple: record which
files were expected and detect missing or truncated downloads. Its limitation is
visible in the <code>abc</code> to <code>abd</code> example: the name and size can agree while the text
differs. That Rust comparison is a deliberately limited baseline, not a claim
that historical dataset projects relied only on file sizes.</p>
<p>A file inventory alone does not preserve a dataset’s collection context,
provenance or suitability for language-model training.
Datasheets for Datasets proposes structured dataset documentation; the later
ROOTS corpus describes source selection, metadata and governance for a
multilingual language-model corpus.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010v8">Datasheets for Datasets</a> was first posted in
<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2018</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2018</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2018</span></span></span></span>. Gebru and colleagues propose documentation covering a dataset’s
motivation, composition, collection, preprocessing, uses, distribution and
maintenance. That documentation supports informed decisions by dataset creators
and users; a checksum cannot replace it.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.03915v1">The BigScience ROOTS Corpus</a> is described in
a <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2023</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2023</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2023</span></span></span></span> preprint. The ROOTS corpus paper describes source selection, metadata
and governance in construction of a multilingual language-model corpus; it does
not validate this chapter’s fixture. The tiny manifest is not an implementation
of the ROOTS governance process or proof of a dataset’s suitability.</p>
<p>Keep selected corpus bytes linked to their source context before downstream
filtering, split construction and training. Byte agreement does not establish
quality, privacy or permission.</p>

<h2 id="read-the-evidence-directly">Read the evidence directly</h2>
<p>A spatial diagram would not make this example’s decisions clearer. The file
table states exactly which bytes belong to each role, and the Rust report records
the changed identity, digest refusal and restart counts directly. Read those
values together: the manifest identifies a complete record, byte verification
checks its files, and the scope field identifies the result as a synthetic fixture.</p>

<h2 id="optional-practice-reproduce-and-explain-the-checks">Optional practice: reproduce and explain the checks</h2>
<ol>
<li>Run <code style="overflow-wrap: anywhere;">size_digest_truncation_and_overrun_are_separate_failures</code> and inspect the
<code>abd</code> case. Explain why its length passes but its bytes are refused.</li>
<li>Run <code style="overflow-wrap: anywhere;">provenance_changes_identity_without_changing_raw_digests</code>. Identify the
records that change when the attribution gains <code>v2</code>.</li>
<li>Run <code style="overflow-wrap: anywhere;">actual_error_body_consumes_budget_without_retaining_payload</code>. Explain why
discarding the error text does not permit a fresh request under the toy ceiling.</li>
</ol>
<details><summary>Checked explanations for the three corpus-verification tasks</summary><ol>
<li>The manifest expects <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3</span></span></span></span> bytes, so length alone cannot distinguish <code>abc</code> from
<code>abd</code>. Their digests differ; the full verifier returns <code>Hash</code> rather than
publishing the replacement as the selected corpus.</li>
<li>The attribution payload entry changes its count and digest, and both source
records change their attribution digest. The raw train and held-out digests
remain unchanged. The complete manifest changes, so its artifact identity
changes too.</li>
<li>The <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> delivered error bytes remain charged. With <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">9</span></span></span></span> raw bytes still needed,
projected delivery is <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">11</span></span></span></span> bytes, above the <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">10</span></span></span></span>-byte ceiling. The refused
request does not increment attempts or create a payload partial.</li>

<h2 id="what-this-supplies-to-the-decoder-pipeline">What this supplies to the decoder pipeline</h2>
<p>The scalar reference remains unchanged. This chapter supplies a way to identify
and verify a complete corpus input before later filtering and tokenization.
The offline example has not acquired TinyStories. Real acquisition needs its
selected source records and approved provenance; Chapter 42’s filtering work
must consume that verified real input, not relabel this fixture as training data.
Verification answers whether the selected record and available bytes agree.
Quality, privacy, contamination and final split selection remain separate questions.</p> </div> <nav class="chapter-navigation" aria-label="Chapter navigation" data-chapter-navigation <h2 id="the-problem-changes-need-a-fixed-comparison-point">The problem: changes need a fixed comparison point</h2>
<p>The previous chapter joined the tokenizer, decoder, training, evaluation,
checkpoint and generation code. Now the course will extend that system. If the
data, configuration and code change together, a changed result no longer tells
you which version you observed. You need a fixed reference that identifies its
inputs and states exactly what its checks establish.</p>
<p>This chapter keeps the small scalar decoder unchanged. It gives that reference
an input identity and a report whose claims stay attached to their evidence.
The identity identifies the fixed inputs. The checks establish which behavior
this execution reproduced. Neither establishes useful laptop-scale capability.</p>
<h3 id="what-the-reference-actually-does">What the reference actually does</h3>
<p>The fixture assigns <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">8</span></span></span></span> documents to training, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> to validation and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2</span></span></span></span> to test.
The decoder has <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1188</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1188</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1188</span></span></span></span> learned scalar parameters and context capacity <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> tokens.
Its primary training schedule and separately executed replay each perform <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">32</span></span></span></span> updates
on full batches of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">16</span></span></span></span> windows, with <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> valid targets per window. Therefore,
each schedule consumes</p>
<span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32\cdot16\cdot4=2048</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">32</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">16</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span><span class="mbin">⋅</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">2048</span></span></span></span></span>
<p>valid training targets. One pipeline invocation includes both schedules: <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">4096</span></span></span></span>
targets altogether. These counts are derived from the frozen full-batch
schedule, not from a new runtime token counter. Evaluation targets and generated
tokens are separate quantities.</p>
<p>The report’s <code>independent_schedules</code> field counts two separately executed copies
of the same schedule from training seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>39</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">39</span></span></span></span>, not statistically independent
seed samples.</p>
<p>The replay agrees bit for bit with the primary training result in this
execution. The selected decoder and frozen bigram then score the same <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span>
overlapping test-window target slots. Their mean negative log-likelihoods are
approximately <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.866087547</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.866087547</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3.866087547</span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.981342714</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.981342714</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">3.981342714</span></span></span></span> nats per slot, respectively.
This known comparison is a regression check: rerunning it can expose changes
in the checked behavior. It is not an independent estimate of generalization.</p>
<p>There are only <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>442</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">442</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">442</span></span></span></span> within-document transition occurrences in those test
documents. Overlapping windows repeat occurrences, so <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1744</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1744</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1744</span></span></span></span> is not a count
of distinct transitions. A separate policy would score each occurrence once,
using the longest available causal prefix capped at four tokens and only its
newest-position distribution. This run does not report numeric mean NLL or
perplexity under that policy.</p>
<p>The checkpoint round trip preserves its encoded bytes, model and optimizer
bits, and tokenizer. The restored decoder reproduces logits for the fixed
<code>At</code> probe, encoded as token IDs <code>[67,118]</code>. Cached and complete-prefix generation
agree on token IDs <code>[260,34,34]</code>: Cyrillic <code>т</code> followed by two spaces. Agreement
checks the two generation paths; those three tokens do not demonstrate useful
language quality.</p>

<p>Here <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∥</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Vert</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em"></span><span class="mord">∥</span></span></span></span> means composition into the shared identity format’s named,
canonical fields, not writing three unframed strings beside one another.
That distinction matters: without field boundaries, different input sequences
can have the same concatenated bytes. The helper orders fields, serializes one
unambiguous record and hashes its complete bytes.</p>
<p>The settings fix eight BPE merges; decoder width, feed-forward width and context

generation seed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>38</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">38</span></span></span></span>; bigram smoothing <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span>; generation temperature <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em"></span><span class="mord">0.8</span></span></span></span>;

settings by their exact bit patterns rather than rounded display text.</p>

<h3 id="what-matching-identities-do-not-prove">What matching identities do not prove</h3>
<p>A matching digest identifies the same canonical input record, subject to the
hash’s collision-resistance assumption. It does not prove that the algorithm
is correct or that a new machine will reproduce every floating-point bit.</p>
<p>The source identity deliberately covers the forty scalar-reference source
files, not this chapter’s reporting wrapper or interface. Toolchain, locked
dependencies and arithmetic environment are recorded separately. A matching
source digest is therefore not evidence that two execution environments match.
The temporary checkpoint path is also outside the input identity; changing
that path does not change the model’s fixed inputs.</p>
<p>Likewise, exact checkpoint reload is narrower than complete job resumption.
This check does not restore every data cursor, in-flight operation or whole-job
continuation state. No laptop throughput is measured here.</p>

<h2 id="history-reporting-conditions-and-measuring-variation">History: reporting conditions and measuring variation</h2>
<p>A language-model score without its input conditions and scope does not identify
what was evaluated or establish which capabilities were checked.</p>
<p><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03993v2">Model Cards for Model Reporting</a> was
presented in 2019. Mitchell and colleagues propose model documentation that
includes intended uses and evaluation conditions; a model card is not itself
proof of quality.</p>
<p>Model Cards describe evaluation conditions and intended uses; later fine-tuning
experiments study variation across initializations and data orders. Reporting
scope and measuring variation answer different questions.</p>
<p>In <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06305v1">Fine-Tuning Pretrained Language Models: Weight Initializations, Data Orders, and Early Stopping</a>,
published in 2020, Dodge and colleagues study fine-tuning variability associated
with initialization and data order for pretrained language models. This does
not measure variability in the course’s tiny decoder.</p>
<p>Keep a fixed regression reference when changing an LLM pipeline, while recording
separately the evidence needed for quality, seed sensitivity and hardware claims.</p>
<p>The Rust reporting contrast uses the same observation. Reading only the mean
NLL with this expression gives a number:</p>
<pre class="astro-code github-dark-high-contrast" style="background-color:#0a0c10;color:#f0f3f6;overflow-x:auto" tabindex="0" data-language="rust" dir="ltr"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#F0F3F6">trace</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">observation</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">final_evaluation</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">decoder</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#FF9492">    .</span><span style="color:#DBB7FF">mean_nll</span><span style="color:#F0F3F6">()</span></span></code></pre>
<p><code>trace.report()</code> also states the evaluation unit, input identity, replay
accounting and limits. It does not retrain a historical model or execute a seed
sweep.</p>

from parsing a previous human-readable report.</p>

<h2 id="keep-the-three-evidence-layers-separate">Keep the three evidence layers separate</h2>
<p>The digest identifies the fixed inputs. The counts and generated token IDs
describe checked behavior on those inputs. The final card keeps future quality,
job-resumption and hardware claims outside the reference’s evidence boundary.</p>

# Chapter 41 evidence and commitments

This is author evidence, not learner prose or a publication verdict. Exact source,
test, output and history-evidence bytes are frozen by deterministic packaging.
The edited contract is a projection to check, not independent evidence.

## C1 — Need and scope

Course-local policy: a selected corpus includes two raw sources and their retained
license/attribution, governed by the frozen Chapter41 record and packet. Rust
DatasetPolicy::synthetic_fixture and validate_manifest implement the offline
scope; tinystories fixes the separately queued production pair. The opening,
metadata, catalog, corpus-bundle definition and handoff must distinguish a
complete identified corpus record from a successful download or a filename.
Do not imply cleaning, final splits, quality, privacy or rights are established.
The previous scalar reference is unchanged. The fixture is not TinyStories.

## C2 — Exact byte example

Observed Rust: demo constants TRAIN, VALIDATION, LICENSE and ATTRIBUTION;
run_fixture; exact expected.txt; canonical_fixture_matches_independently_planned_bytes_and_digest.
Derivation: byte counts3,6,13,24; raw3+6=9; payloadtotal3+6+13+24=46,
excluding the separate manifest record.
One newline escape represents one byte. Two source records share metadata files
counted once; raw/valid.txt is not a final course split. File table, nearby prose,
worked_inputs, report caption and optional tasks must carry those units/roles.

## C3 — Manifest and identity

Executable: canonical_manifest_bytes, parse_dataset_manifest, artifact_id;
closed typed Serde records; noncanonical_unknown_and_duplicate_manifest_fields_refuse;
exact canonical digest569de16c16720f73aca07de6a3184b779b80700c3f5f8eefc01f60fea3019b89.
Canonical object fields are declared byte-sorted; arrays retain required order;
compact UTF8 plus oneLF. Incoming bytes must equal reencoding; this is rejection,
not silent normalization. Formula hashes the whole manifest, not raw concatenation
and not a self-included digest. Raw bytes affect identity through recorded counts
and digests; actual payloads still need verification. Hashes are supporting
plumbing, not signatures, permission/privacy/quality assurance or acquisition
evidence. Formula symbols, canonical-manifest/artifact-identity definitions,
solution section and metadata must preserve this distinction.

## C4 — Complete file admission

Executable: DatasetPolicy::validate_manifest, Directory no-follow/regular-file
checks, check_inventory, verify_bundle, verify_payload, publish_bundle,
replay_bundle. Tests: missing_heldout_provenance_and_changed_revision_refuse;
all_four_files_are_required_and_unlisted_files_refuse;
symlink_and_hardlink_payloads_refuse_without_following;
publication_and_replay_reverify_complete_payload.
Order: selected-source/metadata policy, exact inventory, streamed count/digest.
Regular files must have one link. Every file must pass; no partial-pair success.
Publication verifies/fsyncs all owned candidate bytes before same-parent rename;
failed/corrupt existing entries are not overwritten. Replay rechecks bytes, not
future immutability or the later execution mount policy. Learner code caption,
ordered admission list and same-size explanation must use this bounded meaning.

## C5 — Independent failures and provenance variation

Observed: size_digest_truncation_and_overrun_are_separate_failures;
provenance_changes_identity_without_changing_raw_digests; run_fixture report.
Three-byte abd passes length-only equality but produces Hash under abc's expected
digest. Attribution v2 is27bytes; count/digest plus both source references change;
raw digests unchanged; total49bytes. Digest of the consistent variant is
bb4cd61a666c474f893ca2a9027005f00155b2f6fa573010188aa48258723305.
This is a course-local contrast, not an attributed historical project method.
Both worked-change sections and their optional exercise answers must distinguish
size, raw-file digests and whole-record identity.

## C6 — Interruption and charged delivery

Executable: AcquisitionProgressV1, ProgressStore::{create,restore,begin_request,
receive,acknowledge_eof,finish_file,cancel_body}, admit_response;
settled_prefix_resume_preserves_attempts_budget_and_deadline;
unfinished_grant_is_charged_once_across_repeated_recovery;
actual_error_body_consumes_budget_without_retaining_payload;
full_prefix_without_eof_is_not_a_completed_source;
corrupt_prefix_and_progress_are_not_silently_restarted.
Prefix ab2bytes → exact206range bytes2-2/3 with same strongETag → c → bodyEOF
→ finaldigest → separately validate heldouthelloLF. Observed attempts[2,1],
acknowledged9, uncertain0. Full prefix alone is not EOF. A strong ETag binds
responses, not selected-source authenticity; finalSHA binds assembledbytes to
trusted selected policy. Durable grants precede transport; discarded delivered
bodybytes stay charged; uncertain grant is conservatively charged once across
restart; attempts/deadline do not reset. Toybudget2+9=11>10 stops beforedispatch.
Meter is body-interface delivery, not all buffered physical network ingress.
Corrupt regular prefixes quarantine, failure persists; no auto reset.
Restart prose, retained-prefix definition and budget exercise/answer must carry
conditions and distinct quantities. No actual production download occurred.

## C7 — Historical claims

Primary evidence: history-sources.md, exact arXiv versions and section locators.
SRC-DTH-DATA-01 Datasheets for Datasets firstposted2018/published2021 proposes
dataset documentation across seven lifecycle topics. SRC-DTH-DATA-05 ROOTS
arXivv1posted2023 describes source selection, metadata and governance in corpus
construction. Neither implements this Rust manifest nor certifies this fixture.
History source claims, titles, URLs, year meanings and explanatory paragraphs
must remain within those bounded primary claims. No pasted dataset excerpts,
corpus acquisition or third reference is introduced.

## C8 — Presentation and practice

Course-local teaching choice: small exact file table, Rust verifier/report and
checked comparisons explain record relationships more directly than a spatial
diagram. No registered figure. Problem-first explanatory opening; no student
prediction anywhere. Optional reproduce/inspect/explain tasks have checked
answers and are not prerequisites for understanding. Diagram rationale is about
information, not build machinery. Publication is EN-only; no RU surface or stub.
Every table header identifies its column's role/unit, code caption names its
operation/evidence scope, contextual heading orients within its actual section,
and standalone description states corpus/provenance/verification scope locally.

Establish the need for provenance plus byte checks, with explicit exclusions for cleaning, final splits and corpus suitability, without asking for predictions.
reading.value: The problem: a downloaded file does not identify a training corpus An LLM learns from the text supplied to its training pipeline. A filename alone does not tell you which text was supplied. Two files named train.txt can contain different bytes, and a complete download can still come from the wrong source revision. Even the right text is insufficient for a reproducible corpus record if its source, license text or attribution has been lost. The acquisition boundary needs two kinds of evidence together: a record of the selected sources and their provenance, and checks that the available files match that record. This chapter builds that boundary. It does not clean the text, choose final training splits or establish that the corpus is safe or useful.

reading.roleRequirement: This example reading-order section must identify the course-authored offline fixture, the two raw sources and shared provenance payloads, literal newline meaning, raw versus payload byte counts and shared-file accounting. Clarify the fixture's permission and raw-held-out scope without asserting production acquisition.
reading.value:
Start with a complete, tiny corpus bundle The example uses course-authored test bytes, not a downloaded training dataset. It has two raw text sources and two shared provenance files: File in the bundle | Exact bytes represented as a Rust literal | Byte count raw/train.txt | b"abc" | 3 raw/valid.txt | b"hello
" | 6 provenance/LICENSE.txt | b"fixture-only
" | 13 provenance/ATTRIBUTION.txt | b"course-authored fixture
" | 24 In these literals, 
 represents one newline byte, not a backslash followed by the letter n. The two raw sources contain 3+6=9 bytes. The four payload files in the table contain 3+6+13+24=46 bytes; this count excludes the manifest record introduced below. Both source records refer to the same license and attribution files, so those shared files are counted once in the inventory. The fixture’s license identifier is LicenseRef-Course-Test-Only. Its records mark redistribution as not-approved. Those values describe this test fixture; they do not grant permission for a real corpus or a model trained from one. Likewise, the name valid.txt identifies a raw held-out source here, not the final validation split that a later chapter will construct.

reading.roleRequirement: This solution reading-order section must explain the manifest's payload/provenance linkage, exact canonical representation and rejection of alternative representations, then identify the bundle-record digest formula and the bytes it hashes.
reading.value: The solution: identify the record, then verify every file A manifest is the record describing the bundle. Each payload entry names a relative path, a role, a media type, an exact byte count and a SHA-256 digest. Each source record also identifies the selected source revision, requested URL, resolved endpoint, license and attribution. These fields connect a source to its bytes and provenance instead of leaving them as unrelated notes. The manifest receives one fixed byte representation: compact UTF-8 JSON, object keys in byte-sorted order, declared array order and exactly one final newline. That representation is called canonical. Its purpose is to prevent harmless formatting choices, such as indentation, from giving the same record multiple identities. An incoming manifest with a different representation is rejected; the verifier does not quietly rewrite it. The bundle identity is \mathrm{artifact\_id}=\operatorname{SHA256}(\mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes})

reading.roleRequirement: This reading-order section must define the identity formula's quantities and limits, distinguish recorded digests from verification of actual files, explain ordered source-policy/inventory/byte checks and the supporting-library boundary, and connect the actual Rust excerpts and checked corruption/provenance examples to their observed report without implying a real acquisition.
reading.value: What the identity formula means Here \mathrm{canonical\_manifest\_bytes} means the complete canonical record, including the payload digests and source provenance. \operatorname{SHA256} maps those bytes to a 256-bit digest. \mathrm{artifact\_id} is that digest, usually displayed as 64 hexadecimal characters. It identifies the record; it is not a signature or a certificate of legal permission, privacy or language quality. The raw files are represented in the identity through their recorded byte counts and digests. The verifier must still read the actual files and compare them with those entries. Hashing a manifest does not prove that its claimed files exist. The verifier performs three checks in order: Validate the manifest against the selected source policy, including both raw sources and their provenance references. Check the payload inventory. All four listed files must exist as regular, non-linked files; missing or unlisted files cause refusal. Read each file in bounded chunks, count its bytes and calculate its digest. Accept the bundle only when every count and digest matches. SHA-256 calculation and JSON parsing use supporting libraries. Rust owns the course-specific source policy, inventory checks, byte comparisons and admission decision. Rust checks the observed byte count and digest separately, reading at most one bounded chunk at a time and probing for actual end of file. rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/artifact/inventory.rs#bounded-payload-verification pub fn verify_payload( expected: &PayloadEntry, reader: &mut impl Read, ) -> Result<VerifiedPayload, AcquisitionError> { let mut hasher = Sha256::new(); let mut buffer = [0_u8; STREAM_BUFFER_BYTES]; let mut total = 0_u64; loop { // Once expected bytes have arrived, one additional byte distinguishes // a real EOF from a same-prefix oversize object. Never retain that byte. let remaining = expected .bytes .checked_sub(total) .ok_or(AcquisitionError::Size)?; let allowance = remaining.min(STREAM_BUFFER_BYTES as u64) as usize; let count = loop { match reader.read(&mut buffer[..allowance.max(1)]) { Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue, result => break result.map_err(|_| AcquisitionError::Io)?, } }; if count == 0 { break; } total = total .checked_add(count as u64) .ok_or(AcquisitionError::Size)?; if total > expected.bytes { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } hasher.update(&buffer[..count]); } if total != expected.bytes { return Err(AcquisitionError::Size); } let digest = format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize()); if digest != expected.sha256 { return Err(AcquisitionError::Hash); } Ok(VerifiedPayload { path: expected.path.clone(), bytes: total, sha256: digest, }) } Two changes that expose the boundary Replacing b"abc" with b"abd" preserves the train file’s 3-byte length. A size-only check accepts the replacement. The full verifier rejects it with Hash, because the observed digest differs from the selected manifest entry. This is a file-byte check, not evidence about what either text would teach a model. Changing the attribution file to b"course-authored fixture v2\n" instead changes that file to 27 bytes. Rebuilding a consistent manifest updates its attribution entry and both sources’ attribution references. The resulting bundle identity differs, although the two raw text digests remain unchanged. The new complete payload totals 49 bytes. The identity therefore distinguishes provenance changes as well as raw-text changes. Selected fields from the actual offline fixture report are shown below. The manifest occupies 3084 bytes separately from the 46 payload bytes. The scope value keeps this result identified as a synthetic fixture, not an acquired training dataset. { "artifact_id": "569de16c16720f73aca07de6a3184b779b80700c3f5f8eefc01f60fea3019b89", "artifact_manifest_bytes": 3084, "inventoried_files": 4, "logical_sources": 2, "raw_bytes": 9, "scope": "synthetic-offline-fixture", "total_payload_bytes": 46 } The offline Rust report separates bundle identity, verified file bytes, restart accounting and the fixture's limited scope. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/lib.rs#governed-report Ok(serde_json::json!({ "artifact_id": verified.artifact_id(), "artifact_manifest_bytes": canonical_manifest_bytes(&manifest)?.len(), "attribution_variant_artifact_id": artifact_id(&variant)?.as_hex(), "budget_case": { "acknowledged_body_bytes": budget.progress().acknowledged_body_bytes()?, "attempts_after_refusal": budget.progress().attempts(0), "ceiling_bytes": 10, "remaining_raw_bytes": 9, "projected_required_bytes": 11, "refusal": budget_refusal.to_string(), "dispatch_permitted": false }, "checks": { "attribution_change_changes_bundle_identity": artifact_id(&manifest)? != artifact_id(&variant)?, "attribution_change_preserves_raw_digests": manifest.sources.iter().zip(&variant.sources).all(|(a,b)| a.sha256 == b.sha256), "complete_bundle_replay_identity": replay.artifact_id() == verified.artifact_id(), "same_size_wrong_bytes_refusal": corrupted.unwrap_err().to_string(), "size_only_contrast_accepts_abd": b"abd".len() as u64 == raw_train.bytes }, "files": verified.files().iter().map(|file| serde_json::json!({ "bytes": file.bytes(), "path": file.path(), "sha256": file.sha256() })).collect::<Vec<_>>(), "inventoried_files": 4, "logical_sources": 2, "privacy_quality_or_redistribution_approval": false, "raw_bytes": 9, "resume": { "acknowledged_body_bytes": store.progress().acknowledged_body_bytes()?, "attempts": [store.progress().attempts(0), store.progress().attempts(1)], "complete_pair": store.progress().is_complete(), "uncertain_body_bytes": store.progress().uncertain_body_bytes() }, "schema_version": 1, "scope": "synthetic-offline-fixture", "total_payload_bytes": verified.total_bytes() })) The example executable runs only this offline fixture and prints its report. It does not download a training corpus. The example runs the offline corpus fixture and prints its checked report; it performs no real corpus download. rust/demos/ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition/src/main.rs#offline-acquisition-example fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { // The executable has no HTTP transport and no production acquisition mode. let report = run_fixture()?; println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report)?); Ok(()) }

reading.roleRequirement: This reading-order section must explain the selected-source prefix resume, byte offset/range and representation-validator conditions, actual EOF and final-digest completion, separate source accounting, charged discarded delivery and durable uncertain grants. Preserve original limits across restart and distinguish interface-delivered bytes from physical network ingress.
reading.value: Interrupted acquisition must not erase earlier work Acquisition can stop between receiving bytes and completing a source. A resumed request must continue the same selected source and preserve the acquisition’s limits; starting a new process must not grant a new byte budget or deadline. In the fixture, the first request retains b"ab", a 2-byte prefix of the 3-byte train source. After restart, Rust rehashes that retained prefix and checks its recorded digest. The next request asks for the byte at offset 2, where offsets start at zero. Its response must cover exactly bytes 2-2/3 and carry the same strong entity tag as the first response. The entity tag is the server’s representation validator; it ties the resumed response to the earlier response, while the final SHA-256 check ties the assembled bytes to the selected source policy. Receiving b"c" brings the retained length to 3 bytes, but completion still requires an explicit end-of-body observation and the final digest check. The held-out source is then checked separately. The report records 9 acknowledged body bytes and request-attempt counts [2,1]: two attempts for the train source, one for the held-out source. A complete train source alone is not a complete pair. Body bytes that were read and discarded still consume the transfer budget. For a separate toy ceiling of 10 bytes, an error response that delivers 2 discarded bytes leaves only 8 bytes available. The two raw sources still require 9 bytes, so the next request is refused before dispatch: 2+9=11>10. Rust reserves a bounded body-read grant before allowing transport to read. If a process stops with an unsettled grant, recovery charges the whole grant as uncertain delivery, once, rather than assuming that no bytes were read. This conservative rule may prevent further acquisition even when fewer bytes actually arrived. It prevents uncertainty from becoming free budget. The counter measures bytes delivered through this body-read interface, not every byte buffered by the operating system or every network packet. Corrupt retained prefixes are refused and preserved in quarantine. Recovery does not reset the attempt count, charged bytes or original deadline. These safeguards make interruption visible; they do not turn a failed attempt into an admitted corpus.
